scope: Browser walking occupancy query cost and foot reach during curb descent. Broad movement realism remains incomplete.
implementation: Resolve a candidate collision height once per occupancy query instead of once per placed object. Preserve bounds, early exit, and fresh heights on later queries.
Allow normal pelvis compression plus the terrain descent beneath the current or planned leading foot, with at most 20 cm additional allowance. Apply the bound before exponential release.
Preserve the existing actual-ground contact thresholds; add seven-rig, three-rate, four-phase 16 cm curb regression.
Keep a separate body-world-speed diagnostic because reachable ankle targets do not establish smooth body movement.

liveGroundContact.scope: Live grounded outdoor residents at the district spawn; actual skinned sole support vertices versus registered rendered surfaces. No route or pose injection.

queryBenchmark.scope: Paired ABBA CPU query benchmark on actual district terrain and sidewalks with sixteen finite obstacles; not a frame-rate benchmark.

district-profile-current.scope: Local Chromium RAF timing with CPU profiler enabled; not a target hardware benchmark.

district-profile-height-after.scope: Local Chromium RAF timing with CPU profiler enabled; not a target hardware benchmark.

profileInterpretation: The isolated query benchmark improves by about 81.5 percent with exact occupancy, object-check count and height-checksum equivalence. Full-scene profiled frame times are variable and do not prove an FPS improvement. These profiles preceded the curb correction.

curbBodyDiagnostic.scope: Sharp 16 cm curb descent at four gait phases on seven production rigs. Hip world speed is a diagnostic of unresolved body-height discontinuities, not a passing motion-quality assertion.

workers.about: I’m Morgan, the style adviser at Alice + Olivia. I help people compare texture, color and proportion. Tell me what you like wearing, and we can start with a fabric that feels right.
workers.story: Two fabrics in the same color can behave very differently. I look at how each one catches the light and falls in a fold before pairing it with anything else.
workers.returning: Wait… Jevica?! You're really here! Welcome to Alice + Olivia. Welcome back to Alice + Olivia. I’m Morgan, the style adviser. Would you like to hear a little more about my work?
